title: A trial crossing
bodyMd:
Before replacing a footbridge, a council built a temporary crossing thirty metres upstream. Pedestrian counts on the temporary structure were much lower than the old bridge's earlier counts. Some councillors concluded that the permanent bridge was no longer needed. A transport planner noted that the temporary crossing could be reached only by a stairway, whereas the old bridge had gently sloping approaches. Residents using wheelchairs or pushing heavy carts had been observed taking a long alternative route.

The planner did not claim to know how many people would use a replacement bridge. She argued that the temporary trial had changed access as well as location. Its low count could not be read as a pure measure of demand for an accessible crossing. A more informative trial would preserve access conditions or measure the journeys displaced to other routes.
